dse_runs.notes: Precision demodulator: max_abs_err <= 2^-20 (~9.54e-07) at >=50 MSPS. Selection rule is min luts_plus_ffs, so area is the primary driver; power_index is secondary. Error budget is tight, so favour high data_width / high n_iter designs; check whether pipelined or pipelined_m families can reach 50 MSPS with fewer LUTs+FFs than fully unrolled. Keep the front well-spread and feasible.

final_text: The `high_precision` spec is finalized. L1: a single `run_dse` call consumed the full 400-evaluation budget (inner architect mapped the front three times, then stopped), returning exactly one feasible non-dominated design — `pipelined_m:data_width=27,n_iter=22,angle_guard=-1,frac_guard=0,rounding=round,m=6` with luts_plus_ffs=2314 (1908 LUTs + 406 FFs), power_index=4.35, throughput_msps=59.9 and max_abs_err=9.53e-07 (2^-20.00), i.e. the error constraint is met right at its boundary and the throughput constraint has ~20% margin; the front collapses to a single point because the 2^-20 error budget is the binding limit. L2: the spec has no system scenario, so `simulate_system` only recorded simulated DDS facts (SFDR 144.6 dBc, SNR 130.3 dB from a 32-bit phase accumulator, coherent 16384-point FFT, tone bin 1297) and left the selection unchanged. L3/L4 via the `ladder` sub-agent returned no recorded rows for this design (a fresh exhaustive W=27 verification is too heavy for a live campaign, and L4 is never run live), and L5 `back_annotate` returned `no_measured_data` with no winner change, so `reexplore` was correctly not called. `finalize` recorded the min-luts_plus_ffs winner above; all cost/throughput numbers are estimates under the M1 calibration while the error figure is exact from the golden model. Note: `remember` reported that memory is switched off for this campaign, so no lesson was persisted.
